html:
A large dam and hydroelectric power station on the Dnieper river at Zaporizhzhia in Ukraine, built from 1927 to 1932. When it opened it was the largest power station in Europe.

It was a showpiece of the Soviet first five year plan and of Lenin's idea that communism meant Soviet power plus electrification. American engineers, led by Hugh Cooper, advised on the work, and General Electric supplied generators. Tens of thousands of workers built it. Its reservoir drowned the Dnieper rapids, which had blocked river traffic since the time of the Vikings, so ships could now pass. Its power fed new steel and aluminium plants around Zaporizhzhia.

In 1941 the retreating Red Army blew a hole in the dam to slow the Germans, and in 1943 the retreating Germans wrecked it again. It was rebuilt after the war. During Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Russian missiles struck the station in 2024 and badly damaged it.
sum: A large dam and hydroelectric power station on the Dnieper river at Zaporizhzhia in Ukraine, built from 1927 to 1932. When it opened it was the largest power station in Europe.
